newsitem.title: ITALY: San Paolo head sees tough year ahead.
newsitem.headline: San Paolo head sees tough year ahead.

text.p: Italy's Istituto Bancario San Paolo di Torino SpA bank faces a tough year ahead, as falling interest rates put increasing pressure on its margins, the bank's chairman Gianni Zandano said.
"1996 was certainly not an easy year and 1997 presents itself as even more difficult," Zandano told the bank's annual shareholders' meeting.
"In recent weeks I have said that there will no longer be any more easy years for banks and I am ever more convinced of the truth of this forecast," he added.
Zandano said that falling interest rates would erode the bank's capacity to realise capital gains on holdings of treasury instruments.
Sluggish income growth was also putting pressure on bank deposits.
"Households, in the context of weak growth in disposable income, will channel an increasing portion of their financial resources into provisions for pensions and insurance," said Zandano.

Italian banks also faced a stiff investment bill as they prepared for the planned launch of European economic and monetary union (EMU) at a time when tax charges and operating costs were fairly rigid, he added.
